items.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 12:43AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to
30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...From noon today to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak this evening and tonight.
items.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 13 at 12:31AM PST until November 13 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, seas 20 to 26 ft at 21 seconds
and south winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt. For the
Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous seas 21 to 26
ft at 19 seconds and south winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to
40 kt expected. For the Storm Watch, seas 15 to 20 ft at 16
seconds and south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 50 kt
possible.

* WHERE...Inner Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
out 10 NM.

* WHEN...Gale Warning, until 10 PM PST this evening. Hazardous
Seas Warning, from 10 PM this evening to 4 PM PST Saturday.
Storm Watch, from Saturday afternoon through late Saturday
night.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds will cause hazardous seas which
could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Brief gusts up to 50 kt are possible late
early this morning.
items.instruction:
A Storm Watch is issued when the risk of storm force winds of
48 to 63 knots has significantly increased, but the specific
timing and/or location is still uncertain.  It is intended to
provide additional lead time for mariners who may wish to
consider altering their plans.
